pair_reads.name: risk appetite
pair_reads.rising_means: the jumpy stocks are beating the calm ones: traders are taking risk
pair_reads.falling_means: money is hiding in the calm stocks: risk is being cut
pair_reads.why_it_changes_the_read: a seventh tide part cut from the same 500 stocks, so it is about appetite and nothing else
pair_reads.facts_basis: no local closes for SPHB: not measured

pair_reads.name: credit against safety
pair_reads.rising_means: lenders are relaxed about weak companies
pair_reads.falling_means: lenders want safety: the classic early warning for shares
pair_reads.why_it_changes_the_read: replaces the tide's HYG-minus-SPY part, which mixes credit with the stock market itself and is frozen at 23 Sep

pair_reads.name: cyclicals against defensives (equal weight)
pair_reads.rising_means: shoppers' wants are beating shoppers' needs: confidence
pair_reads.why_it_changes_the_read: the Hub has no cyclical-against-defensive read; equal weight keeps AMZN and TSLA from carrying it

pair_reads.name: small against large
pair_reads.rising_means: the rally is reaching small companies: wide participation
pair_reads.falling_means: only the big names are holding the market up
pair_reads.why_it_changes_the_read: the INDEXES tab shows both but never subtracts one from the other

pair_reads.name: the rest of the world against the US
pair_reads.rising_means: the rest of the world is beating the US
pair_reads.falling_means: the US is carrying the world
pair_reads.needs_new_fund: none: both served (ACWI / SPY once TR1 lands)
pair_reads.why_it_changes_the_read: breadth and regime are S&P-only today; this is the first world participation line

honest_notes: Four of the five pair reads need no new fund: both halves are served today and only need wiring.

No fund fixes breadth counting. The on-screen count has one stored session (23 Sep) and counts bond funds as names; the provider's whole-market engine is not connected. Funds add participation spreads, not a count.
Five of the six tide parts come from a file frozen at 23 Sep with no builder, so a new fund cannot move the tide until that file has a script.
The bow-tie column EQAL-IWB cannot draw: neither fund is served, EQAL trades about 27 thousand shares a day, and TR1 skipped IWB. Recommend dropping the column.

A world breadth count becomes possible: 5 countries are served today (Japan, Germany, UK, Korea, China), TR1 adds 4 (Taiwan, India, Brazil, Canada) and this batch 3 (Mexico, Australia, Switzerland): 12 countries to count above or below their 50-day average; the 13 LATER country funds would take it to 25.

method.sources: (a) proposal.json spine and reference_funds, gaps.json index_layer_missing and themes_thin, index-layer.json SKIP rows; (b) countries and regions; (c) size, style and equal weight; (d) macro and risk-appetite lines.
method.served_test: every row was checked by script against universe-20261006.json (590 symbols, digest 116c79f2...) and TR1's ten; none is served or pending. Every ADMIT_NEXT row pairs with at least one served fund (asserted).
method.liquidity: LARGE = about 1 million shares a day or more; FINE = about 150 thousand to 1 million; THIN = under about 150 thousand. A THIN fund can fail the provider's settled-close cross-check and hold the whole set, so no THIN fund is in ADMIT_NEXT.
method.facts: each row's facts_basis says VERIFIED (public fund pages via web search, site named), MEASURED (local file named) or FROM MEMORY. first_year is FROM MEMORY unless facts_basis gives a launch date. No paid data API, no live database, no chart API was used.
method.pair_numbers: measured_local is the ratio's % change over the last 126 sessions and the last 20, from closes-6m-20261006.csv; it is null where one half is not served.
method.tree_nodes: IDX_ ids are those in scripts/cohort-tree-loader.mjs (IDX_US_BROAD, IDX_WORLD, IDX_COUNTRIES, IDX_STYLE, IDX_FACTOR, IDX_MACRO, IDX_THEME_FUNDS).
